prerequisites: basic knowledge of chemistry, physics, and mathematics acquired in the secondary school

learning_outcomes.text: to familiarize students with basic chemical terminology

gaining by students the knowledge regarding basic principles and concepts that are fundamental in chemistry, properties of chemical elements and compounds, the structure of atom, and basic states of matter.
to acquaint students with the basic principles of work in a chemical laboratory, practical ability of conducting chemical experiments and preparation of research reports
Knows and understands fundamental principles and laws of chemistry

Knows and understands modern theories of atom and molecule structures, in particular - electron configuration of atoms. Knows how to relate properties of an element to its positioning on the periodic table.
Knows and understands issues related to the solution chemistry. Knows basics of chemical calculations and properties of the main organic compounds.
Can use laboratory equipment and conduct simple chemical experiments. Is able to prepare calibration curves of the measuring systems.
Can perform basic chemical calculations related to the fundamental laws of chemistry, solution concentrations, stoichiometry, and equilibrium states in electrolyte solutions.
Can work well in a team.
Is aware of the impact of chemical compounds on the environment.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental principles and laws of chemistry
Classification of elements and periodicity in properties
Basic principles of work in a chemical laboratory including principles of occupational health and safety
Determination of the current efficiency of electrolysis, electroplated coatings
Solubility of selected salts in water
Determination of the percentage composition of solutions
Measurement of the electromotive force (SEM) of galvanic cells
teaching_methods: Lecture with a multimedia presentation and discussion of examples

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory: execution of laboratory experiments and submitting reports

assessment_rules: The condition for passing the course is to achieve all the required learning outcomes. To credit the course a student has to obtain the required learning outcomes. The student is obliged to execute all experiments included in the curriculum. The laboratory grade is calculated as an arithmetic average of the partial grades (interviews and reports).
